content: Plasma transfusions are commonly administered to critically ill patients, but the majority of their clinical applications lack robust evidence to support their use. Research indicates that plasma transfusions do not effectively correct mild coagulation abnormalities as measured by the international normalized ratio (INR). Furthermore, in patients who are not experiencing massive bleeding, plasma transfusions appear to be independently associated with worse clinical outcomes. Current guidelines recommend restricting plasma transfusions to patients who are actively bleeding or at significant risk of bleeding, provided they also exhibit moderately abnormal coagulation test results. The aim of this review was to evaluate whether adopting a restrictive versus a liberal plasma transfusion threshold impacts mortality or morbidity in critically ill patients. Additionally, the review sought to assess the clinical effects of varying plasma transfusion thresholds in this population. A comprehensive search for relevant studies was conducted on August 15, 2013. This search included databases such as the Cochrane Injuries Group Specialised Register, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), MEDLINE, EMBASE, and other related resources, including trial registries and reference lists. The inclusion criteria for this review were randomized clinical trials that compared the effects of two plasma transfusion strategies—one using a restrictive threshold and the other a liberal threshold—based on at least one coagulation test in critically ill patients. Data extraction and trial quality assessment were performed independently by two reviewers, following the standard methods outlined in the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions. Out of 843 references identified during the search, none of the trials met the predefined inclusion criteria. As a result, no studies were included in this review. The authors concluded that there is a significant lack of evidence to guide plasma transfusion practices in critically ill patients. Randomized controlled trials are urgently needed to establish the most appropriate plasma transfusion strategies for this patient population.
